newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani premier denies chief justice's pressure.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani premier denies chief justice's pressure.

text.p: Pakistan's caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid on Thurday denied a resigning minister's charge that Chief Justice Sajjad Ali Shah had put pressure to have a nominated judge appointed as the law ministry secretary.

Former law, justice, human rights and parliamentary affairs minister Fakhruddin Ibrahim had made the charge on Wednesday when he resigned his office, citing differences with Khalid and President Farooq Leghari.

A statement issued by Khalid on Thursday said Shah "has not, at any stage, put any pressure on the government to appoint, or not to appoint, any serving or retired judge as the federal law secretary".
Ibrahim had said in his resignation letter that he could not understand why the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court insisted on the appointment of his nominee as secretary to the law ministry.
Ibrahim, himself a former judge of the Supreme Court, had also cited "unjustified interference" in his work, disagreement on changes made to new electoral laws for his action.
But a statement issued by Khalid's cabinet after approving the amendments at a meeting on Thursday said it had "not acted under any pressure whatsoever".
Ibrahim's resignation was second this week of a member of the caretaker cabinet.
On Monday the Minister for Education, Science and Technology and Tourism, Syeda Abida Hussain, resigned to contest a general election set for February 3.

Ibrahim joined the caretaker cabinet after Leghari dismissed prime minister Benazir Bhutto's government on November 5 on disputed charges of corruption and misrule, dissolved the National Assembly (lower house) and ordered fresh elections for February 3.
